item.title: Wrist Arthroscopy — 2026-10-03
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Wrist Arthroscopy Literature Digest — 2026-10-03 Pulled from PubMed across the six target journals — JBJS Am, J Hand Surg Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, J Wrist Surg, J Hand Surg Eur Vol, and Hand Clinics. Restricted to wrist arthroscopic techniques and closely related work. Author line = first & senior author; corresponding-author institution listed per article. 10 articles. A thin live week, filled from the queue. The 7-day entry-date window (2026-09-26 → 2026-10-04) returned one qualifying citation — a Journal of Hand Surgery case series on arthroscopic dermal-matrix interposition for wrist chondral lesions. Because that falls well short of the ~5-paper floor, the window was widened. The 30-day entry-date sweep returned seven, and the six beyond this week's paper were all covered in the 2026-09-26 digest; a 90-day publication-date sweep returned 16, every one of which reconciled against PMIDs already covered in this track. Widening the recent window therefore yields nothing new, so this week draws on the backfill queue carried forward since 2026-09-22: nine older arthroscopic papers (2020–2021) that had been screened, judged qualifying, and held for exactly this kind of dry week. These nine are not new publications — they are flagged with their original publication dates below. The standing non-arthroscopic keyword screen was run (per the vocabulary-blindspot rule) across all 57 citations entering these six journals in the last 7 days. One wrist item without any arthroscopy-stem term was pulled and read: the Hand Clinics case report on salvage of the distal radioulnar joint after failed fixation (PMID 42816022), which ends in a Scheker prosthesis — open, implant-based work with no arthroscopic content, so it is not counted. The rest of the week was the November Hand Clinics upper-limb reconstruction issue, brachial plexus and metacarpal papers, and the October Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery discussions and replies. The thread running through this week. Joint preservation, done through the scope, in places where the default answer has been open surgery or a fusion. A dermal-matrix interposition for Outerbridge IV chondral lesions that keeps 17 wrists out of a salvage procedure at two years; a debridement and arthrolysis for Lichtman III–IV Kienböck that holds at five years despite radiographic progression; thermal shrinkage for palmar midcarpal instability that is still working at twelve years; and electrothermal treatment of low-grade scapholunate tears with 90% back to pre-injury function at seven. None of these is a large or controlled series. Together they make the case that "minimal" arthroscopic procedures earn more durable results than their reputation suggests. From our own group: no Wagner-authored paper appeared this week. Journals with no qualifying articles: JBJS Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, and Hand Clinics. The single live paper is from J Hand Surg Am; the backfill papers are from J Wrist Surg (8) and J Hand Surg Eur Vol (1). ---

item.title: Wrist Arthroscopy — 2026-09-26
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Wrist Arthroscopy Literature Digest — 2026-09-26 Pulled from PubMed across the six target journals — JBJS Am, J Hand Surg Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, J Wrist Surg, J Hand Surg Eur Vol, and Hand Clinics. Restricted to wrist arthroscopic techniques and closely related work. Author line = first & senior author; corresponding-author institution listed per article. 6 articles. A live week, and a genuinely good one. After last week's backfill digest, the 7-day entry-date window (2026-09-19 → 2026-09-27) returned six citations, all six new and all six qualifying — the entire October 2026 issue of the Journal of Wrist Surgery landed at once. No window-widening was needed. For completeness the 30-day entry-date sweep returned the same six, and a 90-day publication-date sweep returned 10, every one of which reconciled against PMIDs already covered in this track or the wrist-arthroplasty track. The standing non-arthroscopic keyword screen was run (per the vocabulary-blindspot rule) across all 67 citations entering these six journals in the last 14 days. Six wrist papers without any arthroscop term were pulled and read: scaphoid nonunion fixation with headless compression screws (42788187), scaffold fixation of multifragmented intra-articular distal radius fractures (42788181), dorsal lunate dislocation systematic review (42787919), revision rates after scapholunate repair/reconstruction in PearlDiver (42787912), scaphoid morphology after nonunion fixation (42788150), and delayed DRUJ dysfunction after paediatric forearm fractures (42788182). None contains arthroscopic technique content — all are open, radiographic, or administrative-database work — so none is counted. The SL revision-rate database study (1,320 patients, 5-year follow-up) is the one worth knowing about as background for the reconstruction papers below, and it is flagged here rather than in the digest proper. The thread running through this week. Two independent Australian series arrive at the same conclusion from different directions: dorsal-ulnar TFCC pathology does not travel alone. In the Sydney dorsal-TFCC cohort, 55% had concurrent scapholunate instability; in the Perth ECU series, six of seven had a concurrent dorsal peripheral TFCC tear or SL instability requiring arthroscopic repair at the same sitting. Both groups make the same practical argument — the ulnar-sided wrist that hurts on pronosupination is usually a multi-structure injury, and a scope that only looks where the MRI pointed will under-call it. The MRI numbers in the first paper are the ones that will stick with you: dorsal TFCC tears correctly identified in 14%, and the TFCC read as entirely normal in 48%. From our own group: no Wagner-authored paper appeared this week. Journals with no qualifying articles: JBJS Am, J Hand Surg Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, J Hand Surg Eur Vol, and Hand Clinics. All six qualifying papers are from the Journal of Wrist Surgery October 2026 issue. --- Journal of Wrist Surgery (6) Clinical, R

Two is below threshold, so the window was widened. How it was widened. The search was repeated by publication date as well as entry date, per the standing rule. The 90-day dp sweep returned 15 citations against 4 by 30-day edat; all 13 prior ones were already covered in earlier digests, leaving the same two. A MeSH-broadened sweep (arthroscopymh + wrist jointmh / carpal jointsmh / triangular fibrocartilagemh, 4 months by publication date) returned 28 citations and added nothing new — the search strategy is not the limiting factor. The Washington University foveal TFCC repair outcomes paper (Hong/Goldfarb, below) does not carry arthroscop anywhere in its title or abstract — it describes the ulnar tunnel foveal repair by technique name only — so the primary query missed it entirely. item.description: Weekly Wrist Arthroscopy Literature Digest — 2026-07-26 Pulled from PubMed across the six target journals — JBJS Am, J Hand Surg Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, J Wrist Surg, J Hand Surg Eur Vol, and Hand Clinics. Restricted to articles focused on wrist arthroscopic techniques. Author line = first & senior/corresponding author; corresponding-author institution listed per article. No new qualifying articles this week. A 7-day and a 30-day PubMed entry-date (edat) search across all six journals both returned zero newly-indexed citations. The window was widened again to the full prior 90 days (by both entry date and publication date), cross-referenced against all four prior digests (2026-07-03, 2026-07-04, 2026-07-11, 2026-07-18). Every candidate PMID surfaced was already accounted for: - The 90-day entry-date pool contained only four PMIDs — 42246463, 42179684, 42093184, 42059558 — the same four flagged in the 2026-07-18 run. The first three were featured on 2026-07-03; the fourth (bilateral dynamic CT for scapholunate instability, Plast Reconstr Surg) remains excluded as a diagnostic-imaging protocol study in which arthroscopy serves only as the reference standard, not the technique under study. - A 90-day publication-date search returned 20 PMIDs; each one maps to an article already featured in the 2026-07-03 (18 articles) or 2026-07-04 digest. None is a newly-qualifying wrist-arthroscopy technique paper that a prior week missed. This is the fifth consecutive week without new material in this niche literature — J Bone Joint Surg Am, J Hand Surg Am, Plast Reconstr Surg, J Wrist Surg, J Hand Surg Eur Vol, and Hand Clinics all had zero newly-qualifying wrist-arthroscopy citations for the 7- and 30-day windows. Because there is nothing new to report, this week's podcast episode is again a thematic round-up of the 24 wrist-arthroscopy articles surfaced across the program so far (2026-07-03 through 2026-07-11) — this time reframed by evidence maturity (practice-ready vs promising-but-unproven) and by the concrete clinic decisions each paper actually informs, rather than by journal or by anatomical theme. See Episodes/2026-07-26 Tutor Wrist.txt. No new author-outreach drafts were created this week (see Outreach/2026-07-26 Outreach.md). --- Generated automatically from PubMed via NCBI E-utilities. This track runs weekly over the prior 7 days, widening the window when the literature is thin — as it has now been for five consecutive weeks.
